reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) shows SPS densification of metal diborides at 2000 °C, not 1800 °C, and for high-entropy compositions, not single-phase ZrB2. No evidence supports the specific protective liner scheme, the link between reduced porosity and plating bath resistance, or the feasibility of the lower temperature for pure ZrB2.
premises: SPS can densify ZrB2 at ~1800 °C, well below conventional sintering temperatures (>2300 °C)
Short SPS dwell times (<10 min) and rapid heating prevent excessive grain growth and pore coarsening
A Mo foil liner with graphite paper prevents contamination and ensures uniform heating during SPS
Reduced porosity from SPS directly improves mechanical integrity and resistance to liquid plating bath degradation
